messages:
maria: Quick sync — ran profiler on nightly build (TP=2, PP=4). Seeing repeated all-reduce spikes when KV cache stripes cross PP boundaries, stalls line up with kvcache loads.

jason: can you paste the perf trace?

maria: ```trace
GPU0: kvcache_load -> kernelA -> all_reduce(256KB) -> kernelB
GPU1: cache_miss -> all_reduce wait
```

kevin: hmm sounds like our batching heuristic is coalescing prefixes that create imbalanced seq lengths. did you try turning off auto-batch for kv reads? :thinking:

maria: yes, disabling prefix-batch reduces stalls but drops throughput ~8%.

sara: any numbers on comm/compute overlap? have we tried async all-reduce + scheduler tweak?

maria: overlap currently ~30% effective. Async all-reduce + NCCL_GROUP gets us to ~60% on short sequences but increases peak HBM.

jason: could we move kvcache shards into DP across PP ranks? that would avoid cross-PP all-reduces for cache hits but needs KV replication.

kevin: tradeoffs: DP => no all-reduce for kvcache but more memory per replica. TP helps compute parallelism but complicates shard ownership and increases cross-stage traffic.

sara: proposal: hybrid sharding — replicate hot prefixes (DP) and shard cold prefixes across PP/TP. Choose hot set with runtime LFU window.

maria: prototyped this morning. hot set replicated across PP ranks. results: p50 latency -4-6%, p95 -12%, but HBM +20%. All-reduce count for kvcache ops down ~45%.

perf-bot: nightly vs baseline checks:
- tokens/sec p50: +3%
- latency p95: -12%
- HBM peak: +22%

jason: nice. ops runbook needed: if memory > threshold, fallback to full sharding and enable async all-reduce.

kevin: also need kernel selector tweak: prefer non-blocking kvcache kernel when async all-reduce enabled to improve overlap.

sara: can someone post the config diff so eng-sre can smoke test? @maria

maria: pasted config diff below:
```yaml
kvcache:
  sharding: hybrid
  hot_replication_threshold: 0.02 # top 2% prefixes
  async_allreduce: true
  kernel_mode: non_blocking_when_async
```

ops-bot: scheduled canary deploy to gpu-pool-3 at 2025-11-20T04:00Z :rocket:

jason: next steps: 1) run perf matrix across seq lengths 8/64/512, 2) quantify memory vs throughput curve, 3) add hotset telemetry to console. I'll own 1.

kevin: I'll file a small PR to kernel selector with a fallback flag.

sara: I'll draft the canary runbook and set rollback thresholds.

maria: thanks all — follow-up sync Thursday 9am PT. :thumbsup:
